text:
Maya: CI red on PR #3421 after the poetry lock bump — linux wheel job fails with a msgpack wheel build error. Anyone available for a quick triage?

ci-bot: Build failed: linux-wheels-ubuntu-20.04 · job: wheel-build · https://ci.internal/redwood/3421/builds/10234

Liam: Can you paste the failing pip output? My hunch: new msgpack release dropped binary wheels and we’re falling back to source which requires a C toolchain.

Maya: Pasting the relevant snippet from the job: 
```
Building wheel for msgpack (pyproject.toml) ... error
  error: subprocess-exited-with-error
  × Building wheel for msgpack failed with error code 1
  │   clang: error: unknown argument: '-fstack-clash-protection'
  │   note: cc1plus: error: unrecognized command line option '-fstack-clash-protection'
  --> [end]
```

Olga: That -fstack-clash-protection flag suggests the build system expects a newer toolchain or a different compiler. Which msgpack version got pulled in by the lock bump?

Maya: Lock bump came from Dependabot-like job — it moved msgpack from 1.0.2 -> 1.0.3 in the lockfile. I didn't touch native deps.

Sam: If 1.0.3 removed manylinux wheels for our target platform, pip will try source and then the C compile fails on our build image. Quick workaround is to constrain msgpack to 1.0.2 in the pyproject or a constraints.txt and re-run CI.

Liam: Agree. Before pinning, we can bisect the lock bump locally to confirm it's the msgpack change. Steps: checkout the commit before the lock bump, run `poetry lock && poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes -o reqs.txt && docker run --rm -it python:3.10-slim bash -c "pip install -r reqs.txt"` — should reproduce.

Maya: I reproduced locally with the same docker image; it fails. Running the pip build in an interactive container shows the same clang flag error.

Olga: Short-term fix: add a pinned constraint. Long term: we should decide policy on transitive C-extension pinning and add a CI gate that ensures binary wheels exist for ubuntu/generic targets.

Maya: I pushed a tiny patch to PR #3421 that adds a constraints file and pins msgpack==1.0.2. Pushed as `fix(ci): pin msgpack to avoid source builds`. CI queued.

ci-bot: Rerun queued: linux-wheels-ubuntu-20.04 · build 10235.

Sam: If the constrained job passes, we should merge the pin as a hotfix and open a follow-up to revert once upstream publishes compatible wheels or we fix our toolchain. Also consider adding a smoke job that runs a pip-only install to detect missing wheels early.

ci-bot: Build passed: linux-wheels-ubuntu-20.04 · build 10235 ✅

Liam: Nice. I'll open an eng-infra issue describing the incident (binary wheel availability, ubuntu image surface area) and propose: 1) add a constraints check job, 2) add a transitive-C-extensions policy page, 3) run a periodic job to validate common wheel availability.

Olga: Also check our manylinux wheelhouse mirror — some wheels were yanked upstream recently. Might be worth caching commonly used wheels for reproducibility.

Maya: Thanks all — resolving for now. I'll add a note to the PR and create a follow-up card. :white_check_mark: 

Sam: +1. Tag me on the eng-infra issue and I’ll write up the proposed CI changes.
